about.title: Santa Ana Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Ana is home to roughly 335,400 people and sits at the center of Orange County, which means a steady flow of patients moving through local clinics, urgent care, and emergency departments. Most of that care goes the way it should. Sometimes it does not. A missed diagnosis, a medication mix-up, a surgical step skipped, a lab result nobody followed up on — these are the situations California treats as possible medical malpractice, but only when a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that failure caused harm. An unwanted result by itself is not enough. Under MICRA, the timeline is tight: generally one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, with a 90-day notice sent to the provider before any lawsuit. Because a qualified medical expert is nearly always needed to explain what went wrong, early review matters. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Santa Ana residents with an independent attorney who takes these claims on contingency.

items.question: I was treated at a Santa Ana emergency room after a crash on Bristol Street. Could my worsening condition be malpractice?
items.answer: Possibly, but it depends on what the ER did and did not do. Santa Ana recorded 1,708 injury collisions in 2025, so local emergency departments see many crash patients, and a missed fracture or overlooked internal bleeding can qualify as malpractice if the standard of care was not met. The crash itself and the medical error would be separate claims, and an attorney can sort out which applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury. There is also an outer limit of three years from the date the harm occurred, regardless of discovery. You must also give the provider 90 days' written notice before filing suit, which is one more reason not to wait.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a Santa Ana malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises every year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled differently. An independent attorney can explain how the current figures apply to your claim without anyone promising a particular result.
